Class SsComboBox2<K,D,D2>

java.lang.Object
java.awt.Component
java.awt.Container
javax.swing.JComponent
javax.swing.JComboBox<ListItem>
dev.visdb.seesaw.SsComboBox2<K,D,D2>
Type Parameters:
K - key type
D - displayValue type
D2 - d2 type
All Implemented Interfaces:
RSC, SsComponent, ActionListener, ImageObserver, ItemSelectable, MenuContainer, Serializable, EventListener, Accessible, ListDataListener
Direct Known Subclasses:
SsComboBox1, SsDbComboBox2
public class SsComboBox2<K,D,D2> extends JComboBox<ListItem> implements SsComponent
Provide a way of displaying "text", corresponding to "keys" in a JComboBox . The combo display values are created by an ListItemFormat. If not specified, keys are auto-generated [0-N); and in this case <K> must be "Integer" or "Long". In some applications, a key is a key in some database table, see SsDbComboBox2. There are convenience methods for using an enum for both "text" and "keys", see setDisplayValues(java.lang.Class).

This is the base class for combo boxes; it uses/handles getAllowNull()/setAllowNull(boolean), and tracks metadata changes, for adding/removing nullItem to the item list. In addition, there are JComboBox models for use with or without glazed lists; these models have static methods for hooking things up to the JComboBox, see SsComboBox2.ModelType, which is used with Builder.modelType(modelType) to select the model type.

See DBComboBox2 examples of working with Builders.

Warning: This combo box automatically inserts an item when getAllowNull() is true. This comboBox may use GlazedLists which dynamically changes the contents of the combo box list. Do not use methods that are based on index in the combo box list, unless you're sure... For example use getChosenKey() not something that is based on getSelectedIndex(). Change the current/selected combo box item with methods such as setChosenKey(K) and setChosenDisplayValue(D). Use the methods hasItems() and hasSelection() which take into account getAllowNull().

Notice that: getChosenKey() returns null in two situations related to getAllowNull()

  • nothing is selected in this combo box
  • the nullItem is selected in this combo box

getSelectedItem() == null indicates there is no combo box selection; it is different than !hasSelection() when getAllowNull() is true.

If subclasses need to work directly with the combo box model, refer to KeyDisplayValueSwingModel and especially KeyDisplayValueSwingModel.Remodel

Here's an example of using auto-generated keys 

SsComboBox1<Long, String> combobox = new SsComboBox1<>() {};
List<String> options = List.of("111", "2222", "33333");
combobox.setDisplayValues(options);
The generated keys start at zero, the key:value pairs for the above are: {0: "111", 1: "2222", 2: "33333"}.

To provide your own keys, set the keys along with the options. 

SsComboBox1<Integer, String> combobox = new SsComboBox1<>() {};
List<String> options = List.of("111", "2222", "33333");
// The keys used in "my_column".
List<Integer> keys = List.of(1, 5, 7);
combobox.setDisplayValues(options, keys);

// Next line is assuming rowsModel has been initialized
// and "my_column" is a column in its rowSet.
rowsModel.bind(combobox, "my_column");

Classes that extend this class, should use adjustForNullItem() after clearing the itemList or when a change is made that might affect whether or not a nullItem is required.

Note that if you do not want to use the auto-generated keys, the keys must be set before invoking the bind() method to associate the combobox to a database column.

Initially no D2.

Since:
4.0.0

  • Field Details

    • nullItem

      protected ListItem nullItem
      When getAllowNull() is true, this is the null item; when false this is null. So setSelectedItem(nullItem) does the right thing whether getAllowNull() is true or false.

      When the item list is cleared, for example remodel.clear() the nullItem must be set to null.

    • getChosenItem

      public Item2<K,D,D2> getChosenItem()
      Return a copy of the chosenItem with methods getKey(), getDisplayValue(); if hasD2() there's also getD2().

      Here's an example of creating a non-generic version of getChosenItem(). 

      public class ComboBoxIntString extends SsComboBox1<Integer, String> {
  public static class Item extends Item1<Integer, String> {
    public Item(Integer key, String displayValue) {
      super(key, displayValue);
    }
  }

  @Override
  public Item getChosenItem() {
    Optional<Item> item = getChosenItem((remodel, lItem) -> {
      return new Item(remodel.getKey(lItem), remodel.getDisplayValue(lItem));
    });
    return item.orElse(new Item(null, null));
  }
}
      Returns:
      a copy of the chosen item

    • setMissingDisplayValueControl

      public EnumSet<SsComboBox2.MissingDisplayValueControl> setMissingDisplayValueControl(EnumSet<SsComboBox2.MissingDisplayValueControl> flags)
      Set the flags that control how a Key without a specified displayValue is handled. If MC_ADD and a Key is encountered and no DisplayValue was specified, a combobox list entry is created for the Key with null displayValue; a custom message, see setListItemFormat(dev.visdb.seesaw.models.SSListItemFormat), may be setup for handling these entries for the combobox display.If MC_CLEANUP then when the combobox navigates away from an entry with a missing displayValue, the automatically created list entry is removed.

      Flags default to MC_ADD and MC_CLEANUP.

      Parameters:
      flags - new value
      Returns:
      previous value

    • glazedListArrowHandler

      protected void glazedListArrowHandler()
      When dealing with GlazedLists (1.11) restore expected combo behavior.

      Per GL JavaDoc: AutoCompleteSupport

      4. typing the up arrow key when the popup is visible and the selected element is the first element causes the autocompletion to be cleared and the popup's selection to be removed. 6. typing the down arrow key when the popup is visible and the selected element is the last element causes the autocompletion to be cleared and the popup's selection to be removed

      We want to restore the normal JComboBox behavior of not going past the first or last item. This would be the ideal case, matching JComboBox. If GlazedLists ever changes the arrow key behavior, this can be removed.
